channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: US May Put Missile System on Japan Island Near Taiwan in Drills
item.description: The US military is considering deploying an advanced anti-ship missile system to a Japanese island close to Taiwan for the first time during a major training exercise later this month, a move that may draw China’s ire.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Gale

item.title: Northern Ireland Faces a New Political Crisis
item.description: Another collapse could damage an arrangement that has just about managed to hold a fragile peace for almost 30 years.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Fletcher

item.title: Sweden’s Andersson Gets Fresh Shot at Forming Government
item.description: Sweden’s Social Democrat leader and election winner Magdalena Andersson was asked to have a further go at forming a new government after her first attempt failed.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Duxbury

item.title: Sanchez Triggers Speculation of Another Early Spanish Election
item.description: Spain could be headed to an early general election before the end of the year if, as expected, the government suffers a defeat in Parliament on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: India Renames 28 Ladakh Sites, Risking Fresh China Friction
item.description: India renamed 28 places and geographical features in the northern territory of Ladakh, asserting its claims in a disputed region where the border with China has repeatedly strained ties between the Asian neighbors.
item.dc:creator: Sudhi Ranjan Sen

item.title: Brazil Election to See Lula, Bolsonaro in Tight Race
item.description: Brazilians will vote in an election on Sunday in what polls suggest will be a tight rate between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. If no candidate secures a majority, a runoff will follow on Oct. 25. Adriana Dupita from Bloomberg Economics breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What's Next as US Urges Europe to Release Diesel Reserves?
item.description: The Trump administration is ramping up pressure on the European Union to release diesel stockpiles, a move seen potentially averting a ban on US exports of the critical fuel. "The Europeans, they're sitting on reserves of diesel," said US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in an interview with Bloomberg on Thursday. "They should probably release some of these." Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Switzerland’s Parmelin Will Leave Government at Year-End
item.description: Swiss Economy Minister Guy Parmelin announced his resignation, saying he will leave office at the end of the year, when his one-year term as the country’s rotating president also ends.
item.dc:creator: Bastian Benrath-Wright

item.title: Russia’s Spending Plans Show Putin Preparing for Years of War
item.description: Russia is preparing for the war in Ukraine to continue for years by planning record war spending, abandoning plans to rein in military outlays.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Malaysian State’s Royal Crisis Complicates UMNO’s Electoral Comeback
item.description: A months-long crisis over the monarchy in a small Malaysian state has become a potential stumbling block for the United Malays National Organization, which had been gaining ground on Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
item.dc:creator: Ram Anand and Danial Azhar

item.title: Mass Killings Show the Face of South African Murder Is Changing
item.description: On a recent Saturday night, a minibus taxi drew up to a tavern in the gold-mining town of Carletonville west of Johannesburg. Eight men armed with AK-47 rifles alighted from the vehicle before gunning down patrons. Eighteen people died.
item.dc:creator: S'thembile Cele

item.title: Man City Verdict Puts UK-UAE Diplomatic Relations Under Strain
item.description: A historic legal ruling against Manchester City Football Club has placed diplomatic ties between the UK and the United Arab Emirates under significant strain, with billions of pounds in projected foreign investment at stake.
item.dc:creator: Alex Dooler, Dinesh Nair and Alex Wickham

item.title: Speed of French Bond Rout Is a Concern, StoneX Financial Says
item.description: Shriya Samarth, head of EMEA rates at StoneX Financial, discusses France's fiscal situation and the spread between French and German bond yields. The global bond rout has hit harder and faster in France amid concern about missed deficit targets, policy gridlock and presidential elections next year. "There's a lot of different risks mingling here, and the fact that the spread blew out so quickly is definitely concerning," Samarth tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India Election Panel Seeks to Restore Voters Amid Protest Threat
item.description: India’s Election Commission announced a fresh drive to enroll eligible voters whose names were omitted from electoral rolls during a recent revision, as planned nationwide protests by opposition parties and students intensify pressure on the poll panel over its contentious overhaul.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Srivastava and Sudhi Ranjan Sen

item.title: France Budget Crisis Deepens as Investors Head for the Exit
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Risks spanning credit markets, elevated commodity prices and French political turmoil boosted demand for safer government bonds, snapping a prolonged decline fueled by persistent inflation concerns.
The Pentagon is deploying an additional aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf, according to a US official, a move that gives American commanders more options if President Donald Trump chooses to escalate attacks on Iran.
And Anthropic is seeking to go public as soon as the middle of November, according to people familiar with the matter.
Today guest: Anne-Laure Kiechel, Global Sovereign Advisory, CEO (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Malaysia’s Anwar Loses Another Lawmaker Ahead of Budget
item.description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim lost another lawmaker from his People’s Justice Party after its treasurer Lee Chean Chung resigned from his seat just a week before the tabling of next year’s national budget.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan

item.title: Eritrea Cuts Ethiopian Ties as Horn of Africa Tensions Flare
item.description: Eritrea severed diplomatic ties with Ethiopia and alleged “deplorable acts of hostility” by its neighbor, which is battling a rebellion in its northern Tigray region on their common border.
item.dc:creator: Simon Marks

item.title: Nvidia's AI Chips Reach China Despite US Curbs
item.description: Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips keep making their way to China despite US curbs. Government officials are asking why the company missed red flags, saying Washington’s export controls have spawned a sprawling shadow trade. The company hasn’t been accused of violating controls or willfully aiding smugglers, and said it abides by the rules. Bloomberg's Edwin Chan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Taiwan Gets Two Advanced US Fighter Jets After Years of Delays
item.description: Taiwan received two new US-made fighter jets that will be among the most advanced in its arsenal, taking delivery after years of delays amid growing military pressure from China.
item.dc:creator: Yian Lee

item.title: Hungary-Ukraine Ties Stay Fraught Months After Orban Ouster
item.description: The Hungarian government has no plans to send military equipment to Ukraine, according to the deputy foreign minister, sticking with the policy adopted by the previous nationalist leader Viktor Orban.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Escritt and Marton Kasnyik
